headline_marked: 3,000 [[tourists rescued from Sajek]] after gunfire and road blockade
headline: 3,000 tourists rescued from Sajek after gunfire and road blockade
summary: Army and police escorted stranded travelers to Khagrachhari following clashes between security forces and protesters demanding the removal of an armed group.
details: Around 3,000 tourists were rescued from the road from Sajek in Rangamati after clashes between blockade supporters and law enforcers, followed by a reported gunfight.
The evacuation was conducted by the army and police. Seven law enforcement personnel—five army members and two police officers—were injured during the clashes.
The blockade was enforced by the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to demand the removal of an armed group affiliated with the PCJSS.

According to the ISPR, protesters began throwing bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists. The ISPR further claimed that armed UPDF members fired 30-40 shots, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence.
However, the UPDF spokesperson and the convener of the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee disputed these claims, alleging that security forces used truncheons and opened fire on peaceful protesters.
The blockade convener alleged that more than 57 civilians were injured by security forces and that law enforcers prevented the injured from being taken to hospitals.
The district administration had suspended tourist travel to the valley from Wednesday evening and ordered all tourists to leave the area by 4:00 pm on Thursday.
caption:
3,000 tourists were stranded in Sajek amid gunfire and a road blockade. Law enforcers and protesters both claim the other side fired first.

Around 3,000 tourists were rescued from the road from Sajek in Rangamati after clashes between blockade supporters and law enforcers, followed by a reported gunfight.

The evacuation was conducted by the army and police. Seven law enforcement personnel—five army members and two police officers—were injured during the clashes.

The blockade was enforced by the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to demand the removal of an armed group affiliated with the PCJSS.

According to the ISPR, protesters began throwing bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists. The ISPR further claimed that armed UPDF members fired 30-40 shots, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence.

However, the UPDF spokesperson and the convener of the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee disputed these claims, alleging that security forces used truncheons and opened fire on peaceful protesters.

The blockade convener alleged that more than 57 civilians were injured by security forces and that law enforcers prevented the injured from being taken to hospitals.

The district administration had suspended tourist travel to the valley from Wednesday evening and ordered all tourists to leave the area by 4:00 pm on Thursday.

headline_marked: Sri Lanka [[chase down 430 to beat England]] in Rawalpindi record-breaker
headline: Sri Lanka chase down 430 to beat England in Rawalpindi record-breaker
summary: Despite Harry Brook's fastest-ever ODI double century, Sri Lanka achieved the second-highest successful chase in men's ODI history.
details: Sri Lanka achieved a historic victory in Rawalpindi, chasing down a mammoth target of 430 runs to beat England by two wickets in a high-scoring thriller.
England had posted a colossal 429 for four, powered by England captain Harry Brook, who smashed an unbeaten 202 off just 114 balls, including 21 fours and 10 sixes.
Brook's innings was a masterclass in power hitting, becoming the fastest double century in men's ODI cricket, breaking the previous record held by Shubman Gill.
Despite the record-breaking feat, Brook became the first batter to score an ODI double century in a losing cause, surpassing the previous highest individual score in a loss.
Sri Lanka's successful chase of 430 is the second-highest in men's ODI history, behind South Africa's 435-run chase against Australia in 2006.
The match's aggregate of 859 runs is the second-highest in an ODI match, and eight batters scored fifty or more, equalling the record for most individual fifty-plus scores.
England's total of 429 for four surpassed the previous highest ODI total recorded in Pakistan, and Joe Root became the first England batter to reach 8,000 ODI runs.
The victory for Sri Lanka Lanka's coach Gary Kirsten, who previously held the record for the highest individual score in Pakistan (188*) until Brook's innings.
caption:
A record-breaking double century wasn't enough! Sri Lanka chase down 430 runs to pull off an unbelievable victory over England.

Sri Lanka achieved a historic victory in Rawalpindi, chasing down a mammoth target of 430 runs to beat England by two wickets in a high-scoring thriller.

England had posted a colossal 429 for four, powered by England captain Harry Brook, who smashed an unbeaten 202 off just 114 balls, including 21 fours and 10 sixes.

Brook's innings was a masterclass in power hitting, becoming the fastest double century in men's ODI cricket, breaking the previous record held by Shubman Gill.

Despite the record-breaking feat, Brook became the first batter to score an ODI double century in a losing cause, surpassing the previous highest individual score in a loss.

Sri Lanka's successful chase of 430 is the second-highest in men's ODI history, behind South Africa's 435-run chase against Australia in 2006.

The match's aggregate of 859 runs is the second-highest in an ODI match, and eight batters scored fifty or more, equalling the record for most individual fifty-plus scores.

England's total of 429 for four surpassed the previous highest ODI total recorded in Pakistan, and Joe Root became the first England batter to reach 8,000 ODI runs.

The victory for Sri Lanka Lanka's coach Gary Kirsten, who previously held the record for the highest individual score in Pakistan (188*) until Brook's innings.
